slot.brief: y = product/quotient of trig functions of 2x; simplify using identities before differentiating, then evaluate derivative at a specific angle.

stem: The curve is $y=\dfrac{\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}$. What is the slope of its normal at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$?

verdicts.working: Using \(\frac{\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}=\tan x\), the tangent slope is \(\sec^2(\pi/3)=4\). The normal slope is \(-1/4\).

working:
$\dfrac{\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}=\tan x,\quad y'=\sec^2x,\quad y'(\pi/3)=4,\quad m_{\text{normal}}=-\dfrac{1}{4}.$

Independent check: Using \(\frac{\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}=\tan x\), the tangent slope is \(\sec^2(\pi/3)=4\). The normal slope is \(-1/4\).
solution:
Using $1+\tan^2x=\frac{1}{\cos^2x}$ and the identity $\frac{\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}=\tan x$,
$$y'=\sec^2x,\qquad y'\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=4.$$
The normal slope is the negative reciprocal of the tangent slope: $m_{\text{normal}}=-\frac{1}{4}$.
